name: Ralf Rangnick
scopeNote: Partial dates are used where the day was not found (Ulm start 1997-07 and end 1999-03 mid-March, Schalke start 2011-03, excluded spells). Undated or generalised quotes are given the article year (2021) or kept unverified. Coach role only (sporting-director years at Salzburg/Leipzig 2012-15 and 2016-18 are excluded; facts from them such as the Mane/Kampl 'red zone' 4-2-2-2 at Salzburg are not used as evidence). Counted: Ulm (Regionalliga Sud title 1997/98, Bundesliga promotion 1998/99, ZDF Sportstudio Dec 1998), Hoffenheim (3rd tier to Bundesliga, 2006-2 Jan 2011), Schalke second spell (Mar-Sep 2011, DFB-Pokal), RB Leipzig head coach (2015/16 promotion, 2018/19). Exact start/end dates for Ulm (1997, July assumed) and Schalke (named March 2011) and Leipzig (late May 2015 per a search summary) were not confirmed on a page read; partial dates used. Style terms used by sources: 'Raumdeckung / ballorientierte Gegnerdeckung' (ball-oriented zonal marking) with a flat back four, pressing, Gegenpressing, vertical play. The Leipzig 4-2-2-2 label is contested for 2018/19: Left Back Football describes a 4-3-3 pressing shape switching to 3-5-2/5-3-2 with man-orientated pressing, so '4-2-2-2' fits 2015/16 but not necessarily 2018/19. Squad-building evidence is mostly recruitment policy (very young signings; Hoffenheim 2008/09 starting XI average age 22.2); little direct minutes data was found for Leipzig.
openQuestions: Exact appointment dates not confirmed on a read page: Ulm (1997, possibly earlier in 1997 than July), Hoffenheim 22 June 2006 and Leipzig 29 May 2015 appear only in a search summary of a Wikipedia mirror; Schalke named March 2011, first match 1 April 2011.
Schalke 2011 and Leipzig 2015/16 have almost no in-period tactical coverage in the mined pages; Schalke 2011 and Hoffenheim set-pieces are thin.

Was the 2018/19 Leipzig base 4-3-3 with 3-5-2 variants (Left Back Football) or still 4-2-2-2 (Tifo, goal.com treat it as Rangnick's Leipzig system, retrospectively)? Needs a tier A/B match-level source for 2018/19.

The 1998 Sportstudio words are known only through English translation (Sporf) and summaries; the original ZDF video was not read. Original German wording and the exact broadcast date (December 1998) to confirm.

Excluded spells and reasons: Stuttgart 1999-2001 (sacked in relegation zone, only Intertoto Cup; not mined in depth); Hannover 2001-04 (2. Bundesliga title, little tactical coverage mined); Schalke 2004-05 (runner-up, no coverage mined); Manchester United interim 2021-22 (6 months, results poor, not counted); Austria national team 2022- (ongoing, outside this brief's pages). Consider adding Stuttgart/Hannover/Austria in a later pass if the profile needs them.

The Coaches' Voice line 'i told my staff we had to change formation - we had to play 4-3-3' sits in the Hoffenheim story (start of 2007/08 2. Bundesliga after one point from three games) but the article does not date it; eventDate 2007/08 is inferred.
Gross (mentor) said Rangnick 'only brought in players that were right for playing his way ... mostly young, Under-23s' (via Planet Football/The Athletic): undated, kept unverified.

spellsCounted.reason: Regionalliga Sud title 1997/98, promotion to the Bundesliga 1998/99, the Dec 1998 ZDF Sportstudio zonal-marking/back-four lecture; moved to Stuttgart in mid-March 1999 (taz 1999-06-19; Wikipedia says resigned by end of March).
Back-to-back promotions from 3rd tier to Bundesliga, autumn champions 2008/09, 4-1 vs Dortmund; resigned 2 Jan 2011 after the Luiz Gustavo sale to Bayern.
DFB-Pokal 2011, Champions League semi-final, DFL-Supercup; stepped down 22 Sep 2011 (exhaustion).
Promotion to the Bundesliga 2016; later he was sporting director only.
Third place, best defence in the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal final 2019 (lost 3-1 to Bayern), handing over to Nagelsmann.

spellsExcluded.reason: Sacked in the relegation zone; only the Intertoto Cup; style already documented at Ulm; not researched in depth.
2. Bundesliga title but little tactical coverage found; not researched in depth.
Runner-up and Ligapokal but ended with a sacking; no coverage mined.
Interim six-month spell with poor results; not counted for a recognisable style.
National team, ongoing; outside the club-era pages mined in this run.

sources.title: Ralf Rangnick's exhilarating RB Leipzig (Left Back Football)
sources.evidence: RB Leipzig pressed in a 4-3-3 shape as they looked to deny opposition teams access to the central lines by suffocating the opposition team’s deeper-lying midfielders. The front three looked to cut out direct connections from the centre-backs to the deep-lying midfielders by forcing the opposition out wide and backwards.

sources.title: Ralf Rangnick's exhilarating RB Leipzig (Left Back Football)

sources.title: Ralf Rangnick's exhilarating RB Leipzig (Left Back Football)

sources.title: Ralf Rangnick's exhilarating RB Leipzig (Left Back Football)
sources.evidence: Tyler Adams and Kevin Kampl are crucial to RB Leipzig’s build-up as they will create a triangle with their centre back. Kampl will occupy the wide lateral zone while Adams will occupy the central zone as this gives Leipzig direct access to the wide areas

sources.title: Ralf Rangnick's exhilarating RB Leipzig (Left Back Football)

sources.title: Ralf Rangnick's exhilarating RB Leipzig (Left Back Football)

sources.title: Ralf Rangnick's exhilarating RB Leipzig (Left Back Football)
